topic: Separating Mixtures by Winnowing, Scooping, Evaporation, and Magnets
key_concepts: Winnowing uses wind or airflow to separate lighter husk from heavier grains.
Scooping removes floating oil from water because oil is less dense and does not mix with w
Evaporation separates dissolved salt from water by heating, leaving salt crystals behind.
Magnets separate magnetic iron filings from non-magnetic materials like sand.
Mixtures can be homogeneous or heterogeneous.
Decantation, filtration, and sieving are other techniques for separating mixtures.
Separation techniques have real-life uses in farming, oil spill cleanup, and cooking.
Oil floats on water due to differences in density and polarity.
